beats.text: The first battery was a stack of metal discs and salty cloth.
In 1800, Alessandro Volta stacked zinc, copper and wet cloth, and got a steady electric current.
In 1859, Gaston Planté built the first rechargeable battery, from lead and acid. Most cars still use one.
In the 1880s, the dry cell made batteries portable, and powered the first flashlights.
Then alkaline cells lasted far longer, in toys and remotes.
In 1991, Sony sold the first lithium-ion battery.
Today, lithium-ion powers your phone, your laptop, and electric cars.
Follow to see how everything evolved.
